name: bodypart-tiny

cpu.note: the network alone, scored from cached planes (round 1, R5 and R6); a stack read from DICOM costs its reading and decoding on top, which the cascade's card states
cpu.hardware: 64 cores of an AMD EPYC 9745 host, 256 GB of memory, the archive over NFS 4.2; numpy, 64 processes

gpu.note: the network alone, scored from cached planes; in the served cascade the encoder runs on the CPU in the readers' workers
gpu.hardware: 64 cores of an AMD EPYC 9745 host, 256 GB of memory, the archive over NFS 4.2, card: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB, sm_120) under the lease; torch fp32 (the research build)

limits: New patients, from hospitals and scanners seen in training (round 7: the untouched subjects of iaid, multiple_ms, als, ctrl, broms and nmosd)
Fine mode only: six body_part values; answers at or above 0.897 after the calibration below, abstains below it (0.68 of stacks on round 7 T)
A stack without geometry or without a fingerprint gets no answer (an abstention)
Trained on patient pixels: a site model, never exported, never in a release (record 50 study, section 8)
neck against cervical spine follows G2 as Nima ruled on 2026-09-29; the neck class is rare after it

tested.note: the encoder is certified only inside the head; see that card
tested.claim: as part of bodypart-fusion@r7: fine mode at 0.897 on round 7's test T, weighted error among answered stacks
scored from the plane cache with numpy against the certified run of the day, on the screen: every answer and probability identical (class I)
torch fp32 on the card against the certified run: every answer identical, largest calibrated-probability difference

equivalence.set: the screen role's 18,801 stacks, from their cached planes (round 1, 3.2)
equivalence.note: torch fp32 on the card against numpy on the CPU: answers identical, largest probability difference 0.000522 fine and 0.000472 coarse

intended_use: The image component of bodypart-fusion@r7: six body-part log-probabilities per stack from its 8 mm volume and geometry
